questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
digital rural banking = to lu ka
digital secure access = re vo lu
rural secure growth = vo ka su
banking access growth = to re su
digital rural growth = su lu ka
What is the code for “access”?
questions.explanation: Answer: re. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: digital = lu, rural = ka, banking = to, secure = vo, access = re, growth = su.

questions.stem: E is the mother of A. F is the daughter of A. C is the father of A. How is F related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of A, and F is A’s daughter. Hence F is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: C is the brother of B. B is the mother of A. D is the father of C and B. How is C related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of A’s mother B. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of D. D is the father of F. C is the son of F. G is the sister of D. How is D related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of F, and F is C’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 9th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. New front rank = 9+4 = 13. Back rank = 60 − 13 + 1 = 48.

questions.stem: In a queue of 47 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. New front rank = 11+3 = 14. Back rank = 47 − 14 + 1 = 34.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 91 km north, turns left and walks 204 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 221. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 85 km along the initial direction and 204 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(85² + 204²) = 221 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 72 km west, turns left and walks 76 km, then turns left and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 70 km east, turns right and walks 132 km, then turns right and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 143. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 55 km along the initial direction and 132 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(55² + 132²) = 143 km.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹18000 earns ₹2700 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 19845. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 18000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3300 each. One earns 20% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6416.67. Recover each cost separately: 3300×100/120 + 3300×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 40 and 60 hours. An outlet empties it in 80 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 34.29. Net rate = 1/40 + 1/60 − 1/80 = 7/240 tank/hour. Required time = 34.29 hours.

questions.stem: A container holds 100 litres of pure milk. 20 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain?
questions.explanation: Answer: 64. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 100 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 25%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3000. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New quantity / old quantity = 100/125. Reduction percentage = 25/125 ×100.

questions.stem: A 250 m train moving at 90 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 10.87. Relative speed = (90 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 23 m/s. Time = 250/23.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 16 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+16)/(x+16) = 3/2 gives x = 16. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: The average weight of 27 people is 50 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 78. New total minus old total = (27+1)×(50+1) − 27×50 = 78.

questions.stem: A boat covers 104 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Still-water speed = 13 km/h. Upstream speed = 13 − 4. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 7:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 8 months. A receives ₹168000 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 216000. Profit ratio is 84:24. Each ratio unit = ₹2000. Total = 108 × 2000.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] A fee of ₹20 applies to each in the male category and ₹15 to each in the female category at B. What is the total fee collected (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 38400. Derived data: A: first category 420, second category 280; B: first category 960, second category 1280; C: first category 900, second category 1200; D: first category 640, second category 480; E: first category 540, second category 360. Fee = 960×20 + 1280×15.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] The female category at D is what percentage of the male category at B? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Derived data: A: first category 420, second category 280; B: first category 960, second category 1280; C: first category 900, second category 1200; D: first category 640, second category 480; E: first category 540, second category 360. 480 ÷ 960 × 100 = 50%.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] What is the ratio of the male category at A and B together to the female category at D and E together?
questions.explanation: Answer: 23 : 14. Derived data: A: first category 420, second category 280; B: first category 960, second category 1280; C: first category 900, second category 1200; D: first category 640, second category 480; E: first category 540, second category 360. Reduce 1380 : 840 to lowest terms.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] The combined total at A and D is what percentage more or less than the total at C? Give the absolute percentage difference, rounded to two decimals.
questions.explanation: Answer: 13.33. Derived data: A: first category 420, second category 280; B: first category 960, second category 1280; C: first category 900, second category 1200; D: first category 640, second category 480; E: first category 540, second category 360. Percentage difference = |total(A)+total(D)−total(C)| ÷ total(C) × 100.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] If 25% of the female category at E is transferred to the male category there, what is the new size of the male category at E?
questions.explanation: Answer: 630. Derived data: A: first category 420, second category 280; B: first category 960, second category 1280; C: first category 900, second category 1200; D: first category 640, second category 480; E: first category 540, second category 360. New first category = 540 + 25% of 360.
